church_of_the_east.natures_of_christ:
The Church of the East confesses that the one Christ is perfect God and perfect man: two natures, divine and human, and two qnome, the concrete reality of the Godhead and the concrete reality of the manhood, united in one parsopa of Sonship. The natures are not mixed, confused, changed, divided, or separated. Divinity remains divinity and humanity remains humanity, yet there is one Lord, one worship, and one Son.

The Syriac word qnoma does not mean a second Son. It names the individual reality of each nature. The church therefore rejects both a blending that would make the manhood disappear and any talk of two Christs. The formula two natures two qnome is our own dyophysite speech, formed in the East Syriac schools and in synods such as those that follow Babai, not a borrowing of later western definitions.
church_of_the_east.ecumenical_councils:
The Church of the East receives the first two councils as the shared confession of the faith: Nicaea in 325, which teaches that the Son is of the same being as the Father, and Constantinople in 381, which confesses the Holy Spirit with the Father and the Son. Our fathers received Nicaea at Seleucia-Ctesiphon and pray the Nicene faith.

Later gatherings held in the Roman Empire, beginning with Ephesus in 431, are not binding councils for us. They used words our tradition does not use in the same way, and they were called without the Church of the East. Our doctrine of Christ is set by Scripture, the first two councils, and our own synods, not by a longer list of western or Byzantine councils.
church_of_the_east.theotokos:
The Blessed Virgin is honoured as the Mother of Christ, Christotokos, because the one she bore is the one Lord Jesus Christ, God the Word in our humanity. She is truly the mother of the man who is God the Son. The title guards the integrity of the two natures: what is born of Mary is the human qnoma assumed by the Word, not the Godhead as such coming into being in time.

Theotokos, Mother of God, is heard by many in this church as a phrase that can blur that distinction if it is taken to mean that the divine nature itself had a human mother. Members therefore prefer Christotokos or Mother of Christ. The honour given to Mary is real; the concern is to speak of her Son without mixing the natures.
